text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + timeout rate detected for inference-hosted-api in prod (us-west-2). p95 jumped from ~400ms -> ~1.8s, p99 to ~6.2s. Auto-paging oncall (Anika Patel). Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/timeout-deploy

deploy-bot: Canary deploy r4f9 promoted at 2026-03-15T12:31Z (canary -> 25%).

Anika Patel: I'm oncall and watching. Seeing lots of 502/504 from edge. Pulling traces & logs now. @Lena can you check ingress nodes?

Lena Ortiz: Looking. Ingress LB proxy nodes show connection_count at 95th near capacity, tcp_close_wait / FIN_WAIT growing. Could be connection recycling issue.

Raj Mehta: From runtime side, model workers report normal service times. Backend RPC p50/p90 normal. This smells like gateway keeping sockets open and starving connection pools.

Sam Wu: Multiplexer logs show repeated "no free connection" backpressure. Snippet:
```
2026-03-15T12:34:10Z proxy[edge-12]: dial backend timeout after 30s
2026-03-15T12:34:12Z proxy[edge-12]: conn_pool_wait_ms=12500 pending=42
```

Maya Chen: Customer impact: streaming sessions dropping, some premium customers hitting retries. Status page alarms firing.

Anika Patel: Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback canary -> fastest 2) increase proxy conn pool / crew nodes 3) cordon affected edges and shift traffic 4) throttle new canary traffic. Rollback is quickest. Thoughts?

Raj Mehta: I vote rollback. I can execute. Note: previous version had slightly higher memory, but that's acceptable short-term.

Lena Ortiz: We could cordon nodes, but that's slower than rollback and might leave partial traffic. Rollback seems right.

Anika Patel: Rollback approved. @deploy-bot start rollback of r4f9 -> r2c8 now.

deploy-bot: Ack. Starting rollback at 2026-03-15T12:36:05. Will stream updates here.

incident-bot: Ops checklist: collect tcp/conn state and heap profiles from edges: `/ops/scripts/collect-conn-state.sh --since 12:30` 

Sam Wu: Running collect script. Early output shows many sockets stuck in CLOSE_WAIT / FIN_WAIT on edge-1..edge-6 between 12:33-12:35. Saving to /tmp/conn-state-5098765432.log

Raj Mehta: Revert in-progress. Setting canary weight -> 0 at 12:36:20. Rolling back to r2c8.

Anika Patel: Watching metrics. p95 trending down: 1.8s -> 450ms. p99 down: 6.2s -> ~900ms. Nice.

Maya Chen: Drafting status update for customers: "We experienced elevated timeouts downstream of a recent deployment. We have rolled back the change and service latency has returned to normal. Investigating root cause and will follow up." Publish on status page?

Lena Ortiz: After rollback, conn_pool_waits fell to low single digits. Kernel socket counts also dropping. Suspect change in keepalive/reuse semantics in r4f9 that prevented proper connection teardown under high concurrency. Assigning RCA to Raj + Lena.

Raj Mehta: I’ll own the RCA. Hypothesis: client changed connection header/keepalive handling; proxy created many half-open sockets and exhausted pool. Repro locally with load test next.

Sam Wu: Uploading diagnostics archive: /mnt/diagnostics/5098765432.tar.gz (conn logs + cores).

deploy-bot: Rollback complete at 2026-03-15T12:37:10. Canary removed; traffic back to r2c8.

incident-bot: Pager update: mitigation complete, transitioning to SEV2 (investigating root cause). Next steps: RCA, postmortem, add a canary gating check for conn-reuse regressions.

Anika Patel: Handoff: I'll run the timeline doc and sync with stakeholders at 13:15. Leaving incident open for RCA. @Maya @Lena please take handoff for follow-up.

Maya Chen: On it. I'll coordinate customer comms and post-incident notes. :thumbsup:

Lena Ortiz: I'll work with Raj on the root cause and a rollout-safe fix (and a short-term probe to detect conn-leak patterns in future canaries).

Anika Patel: Thanks everyone. If we see any residual spike reopen here. Closing live mitigation.
